# Filter EngineZ — Documentation

> Filter EngineZ documentation — the 16-rule filter catalog, the acceleration algorithms, a live in-browser playground, and the API reference.

Filter EngineZ is a generic, isomorphic, framework-agnostic TypeScript data filter engine: one engine in the browser, in Node or in a Web Worker, with bindings for React, Svelte, Vue and Angular. This site documents it: one page per filter rule and per acceleration algorithm, each with a simple and an advanced explanation, a playground that runs the real engine on a JSON config in the browser, and the API reference.

## Documentation

- [Filter EngineZ — Documentation](https://docs.filterenginez.com/): A quick start, and the way into the rule catalog, the algorithms, the playground and the API reference.
- [Playground](https://docs.filterenginez.com/playground): Edit a JSON FilterEngineConfig and run the real Filter EngineZ engine against a dataset, right in your browser — the same engine and config that run server-side.
- [API reference](https://docs.filterenginez.com/api): The Filter EngineZ public API at a glance, grouped by area: the engine, the rule factories, composition, JSON config, acceleration and the reactive bindings.

## Rules

- [ValueRule](https://docs.filterenginez.com/rules/value): Passes records whose field exactly equals a single configured value.
- [BooleanRule](https://docs.filterenginez.com/rules/boolean): A boolean-field convenience: passes records whose flag equals the configured value.
- [RangeRule](https://docs.filterenginez.com/rules/range): Passes records whose numeric field falls within an inclusive [min, max] range.
- [NumericComparisonRule](https://docs.filterenginez.com/rules/numeric-comparison): Passes records whose numeric field satisfies a single comparison operator against a value.
- [DateRangeRule](https://docs.filterenginez.com/rules/date-range): Passes records whose date field falls in a range — with live relative presets like "last 7 days".
- [InSetRule](https://docs.filterenginez.com/rules/in-set): Passes records whose field value is in a configured set (a multi-select facet).
- [InSetofSetsRule](https://docs.filterenginez.com/rules/in-set-of-sets): Passes records whose value is in ANY of several configured subsets (super-groups).
- [HierarchicalRule](https://docs.filterenginez.com/rules/hierarchical): Passes records under a selected category — including all of its descendants in the tree.
- [TextSearchRule](https://docs.filterenginez.com/rules/text-search): Passes records whose text field matches a query in one of six modes (substring, whole-word, …).
- [FuzzySearchRule](https://docs.filterenginez.com/rules/fuzzy-search): Passes records whose text field is a close (typo-tolerant) match for the query.
- [RegexRule](https://docs.filterenginez.com/rules/regex): Passes records whose string field matches a regular expression.
- [GeoProximityRule](https://docs.filterenginez.com/rules/geo-proximity): Passes records whose coordinates fall within a radius of a center point.
- [ExistsRule](https://docs.filterenginez.com/rules/exists): Passes records whose field has a non-null value (a "has a value" gate).
- [PredicateRule](https://docs.filterenginez.com/rules/predicate): The escape hatch: passes records for which an arbitrary function returns true.
- [BloomMembershipRule](https://docs.filterenginez.com/rules/bloom-membership): A probabilistic pre-screen: "definitely not" or "probably yes" membership from a compact bit-array.
- [CompositeRule](https://docs.filterenginez.com/rules/composite): Combines other rules with AND / OR / NOT into a full Boolean expression tree.

## Algorithms

- [Roaring bitmaps](https://docs.filterenginez.com/algorithms/roaring-bitmaps): One compressed bitmap per rule; combining filters is a single bitwise AND.
- [Mutual-exclusion graph](https://docs.filterenginez.com/algorithms/mutual-exclusion-graph): Precomputed zero-overlap pairs let the engine skip combinations that can only return nothing.
- [Memoized simulation](https://docs.filterenginez.com/algorithms/memoized-simulation): Every "what if I added this filter?" answer is memoized in an LRU cache.
- [R-tree spatial index](https://docs.filterenginez.com/algorithms/r-tree): A bounding-box tree prunes whole regions before any exact distance is computed.
- [Bayesian suggestions](https://docs.filterenginez.com/algorithms/bayesian-suggestions): A co-occurrence model ranks the filters most likely to be selected next.
- [MinHash + LSH similarity](https://docs.filterenginez.com/algorithms/minhash-lsh): MinHash signatures + LSH bucketing turn "find similar" into a bucket lookup.
- [Bloom membership](https://docs.filterenginez.com/algorithms/bloom-filter): A bit-array + k hashes: "definitely not" or "probably yes", in a handful of bit checks.
- [Inverted text index](https://docs.filterenginez.com/algorithms/inverted-text-index): A word→postings index turns whole-word search into a posting-list intersection.

## Demos

- [React RTK](https://react-rtk.filterenginez.com/): Built with React 19 and @filter-enginez/react-signals. Adds the optional Redux mirror via redux-bridge — the engine stays the source of truth.
- [React plain](https://react.filterenginez.com/): Built with React 19 and @filter-enginez/react-signals. The same app with no store library at all, proving the Redux mirror is optional.
- [SvelteKit](https://svelte.filterenginez.com/): Built with SvelteKit 5 and @filter-enginez/svelte-signals. Runs the isomorphic core in SvelteKit’s own server tier, with a zero-JS SSR fallback.
- [Vue](https://vue.filterenginez.com/): Built with Vue 3 and @filter-enginez/vue-signals. Holds the engine in shallowRef — Vue’s deep proxy would break its signals.
- [Angular](https://angular.filterenginez.com/): Built with Angular 22 and @filter-enginez/angular-rxjs. Zoneless and standalone; consumes the engine’s Observables natively, so the binding is DI only.
- [Vanilla](https://vanilla.filterenginez.com/): Built with plain TypeScript and no framework. /books goes through reactive-signals, /books-raw through the bare core — the pair shows what the adapter buys.

## Landing site

- [Filter EngineZ](https://filterenginez.com/): What the engine is, how to install it, and links to everything else.
- [One filter state in six stacks](https://filterenginez.com/compare): One filter state, opened in every demo app that serves its dataset, through the same `?f` URL parameter.
- [How the engine works](https://filterenginez.com/how-it-works): How the engine filters without checking every record: eight algorithms, animated, with a live benchmark in the browser.

## Source

- [filter-enginez on GitHub](https://github.com/mlilli/filter-enginez): The engine: its packages, its architecture document and its guides.
- [filter-enginez-examples on GitHub](https://github.com/mlilli/filter-enginez-examples): These sites: the six demo apps, the documentation site, the landing site and the UI they share.
- [@filter-enginez on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/org/filter-enginez): Every engine package, published under the @filter-enginez scope.
